newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Taiwan December index of leading indicators rise.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan December index of leading indicators rise.

text.p: Taiwan's index of leading business indicators, which forecasts peaks and troughs in the business cycle, rose for the fourth consecutive month in December, the cabinet said on Monday.
The index climbed 0.4 percentage points to 101.1 in December from November, the Council for Economic Planning and Development said in a statement.
The index of coincident indicators also rose in December, gaining 0.6 percentage points to 101.8 from a month ago.
The council said the economy remained in a "green light" condition, indicating a possible recovery, for the second straight month.

But 22 percent of a sample polling of manufacturing executives said the economy would grow worse, up from 19 percent in November, while 17 percent said the economy would improve, slightly more than the 16 percent surveyed a month earlier.
The rest said the economy would remain unchanged.
Most analysts had expected Taiwan's economy to continue its recovery in the first quarter of 1997.
